resources.string: Two ear photos → a personal SOFA profile. Everything is calculated on your phone; photos are never uploaded.
Experimental method. Compare the result with a standard HRTF at the same volume.
Enter straight-line measurements in centimetres. Width: above the ears. Depth: forehead to back of the head. Do not measure the circumference.
Create a new profile after changing photos, marked points or head dimensions. Export saves the latest completed result.
In exstereo, open sound settings → HRTF → “Import SOFA from PC” and select the saved file. This also accepts profiles created on your phone.

Photograph each ear directly from the side, from about 30 cm away, with even lighting. Ask someone to help.

Remove hair and jewellery from the ear. Place a ruler next to it in the same plane. Leave room around the ear for a 9.5 × 9.5 cm square.

Mark the ear canal entrance and two ruler marks on each photo. Enter the distance between the ruler marks. Check the contours: extra shadows and background lines reduce accuracy.
Internal photo copies, marked points and generated profiles will be deleted. Gallery photos and previously exported SOFA files will remain.

Works offline. Uses only the inference parts of pretrained ITSADIVE. No training takes place on the phone.

The profile is an approximation: a generic VIKING head model, ear filters estimated from contours, and analytical delays. It does not use acoustic measurements of the listener.

Original app code: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Third-party components retain their own licences.
Take the photo directly from the side. Place the ruler beside the ear in the same plane. Hair and jewellery must not cover the ear.
Align the photo with the guide: pinch with two fingers to zoom, drag with one to move. The silhouette is approximate; the ruler sets the calculation scale.
The right ear is mirrored by default. If the original photo is already mirrored, check its orientation.
The helix, concha and ear canal should be visible. Extra lines from hair, shadows and the ruler reduce accuracy.
